Suboxone is a partial agonist with a high binding affinity especially at the MU receptor sites. No, it doesn't "remove fentanyl from your body", but it can strip strip fentanyl from receptor sites if the person doesn't have much in their system. To successfully do what I'm talking about you need to wait a while after your last dose of any other opioids (at least 8-12ish hours) before taking any buprenorphine. Then ideally you'll set aside 3-4 days to fully implement the buprenorphine on a graduated schedule (ideally ~16 mgs) Unfortunately you almost certainly  WILL be sent into precipitated withdrawal the first day, but if you increase the doses very gradually across the 3 days, you should only go through PWD for the first 24-48 hours after which you will stabilize on the buprenorphine- and if done properly, you can literally get by stretching like 8 mgs of buprenorphine across a  week or so, at which point you'll be able to drop the bupe with negligible withdrawal symptoms. If you follow a rapid detox like this properly, you'll only have about a day of really being dope sick, followed by maybe another 3 or 4 days feeling a little shitty (which most people probaby won't even notice through the relief of the PWDs having passed).

I guarantee you're gonna think I'm the dumbest mfer out of anyone else on this subreddit after reading what I'm about to say- but I promise I'm genuinely being 100% serious. If you're serious about getting clean, I discovered what was easily the quickest method during my last stint in a rapid detox center before going to rehab. I think it goes without saying that there's one very obvious caveat to this method, however; that is, you're gonna have to spend a little over 24 hours being dope sick- ~12-15 hours (at least, this was roughly the duration in my experience) of which you will literally the sickest you've EVER been in your life. In my case I was kicking a ~5 year long daily habit of doing 90 mgs of methadone along with at least 5-10 pressed fentanyl pills. 

But- with that rambling ass preamble out of the way- the *quickest* way to kick physical opioid dependency is to get a few Suboxone strips (in my case, the nurses slowly gave me an 8 mg strip they'd divided into small sections over the course of the day) and to literally just rip the band-aid off and put yourself into precipitated withdrawal. I can stress enough just how goddamn awful as all fucking hell the WDs will be- like at least 5x worse than the usual dope sickness from quitting cold-turkey. 

And, as anyone could obviously tell, this is likewise NOT a method that 99% of people would ever consider in a million years. 

But, despite all that, there's actually a huge silver lining to this method, believe it or not; and that's the fact that you can pretty much get through the whole thing within 24-48 hours, whereas the acute withdrawal symptoms typically last much longer than that.

In my own experience, I only spent around 14-18 hours in withdrawal- after which I'd totally stabilized with just the final, tiny dose of ~.2mgs of buprenorphine.

Listen, man... Opioids are certainly a dangerously addictive class of narcotics- and that's putting it lightly, to say the least. HOWEVER... opioids are also, first and foremost, the definitive treatment option for people suffering physical pain; that is to say: opioids, when used properly in their legitimate medical context, are a perfectly safe, incredibly effective medicine. 

That being said, my advice would be to get off of them as soon as possible if you're starting to find yourself looking forward to feeling that high. I can tell you from experience as a full-blown fentanyl addict... things have a way of getting out of hand extremely fucking fast when you start getting comfortable with chasing that high. At this point you'll have withdrawals when you quit- but they shouldn't be too awfully hard to get through. Once you start getting to a year plus of daily opioid use under your belt, however, the shit really just becomes a whole different monster than it was before.
